check.reason: The headline and the take both give a specific figure, '$59 million', that doesn't appear in the real headline ('spent heavily') or in anything provided about the story. Calling it 'estimated' doesn't fix this, because it still presents an unsupported number as the story's fact. The rest passes: the target is PhRMA and the industry, patients aren't mocked, no one is quoted, and the tone is dry and satirical. To fix it, remove the dollar figure, for example 'PhRMA Spends Heavily Teaching Google Why Drugs Cost So Much', or confirm the number against the article and cite it.

pick.title: Pharma’s trade group spent heavily on search ads to sway public opinion
pick.headline: PhRMA Spends Estimated $59 Million Teaching Google Why Drugs Cost So Much
pick.take: For an estimated $59 million in search ads, the industry made sure that people asking why their prescriptions cost so much get an answer from the people who set the price. It's a bold strategy: pay to explain the price, rather than change it.
